text: Continuous integration is a practice where developers regularly add their code to a shared project. Every time they do this, automated builds start, and the system compiles the new code to check that everything works. The next step is running tests, which help confirm that the changes do not break existing features. By doing this often, teams can catch issues early, before they become serious problems. CI pipelines organise these steps into a clear process, from building and testing to reporting results. This saves time and helps teams deliver better software.
